newsitem.title: USA: BPA warns Intertie cuts will harm endangered fish.
newsitem.headline: BPA warns Intertie cuts will harm endangered fish.

text.p: Continued constraints on Pacific Intertie power lines, running from the Northwest to California, will have serious consequences for endangered fish species, the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Thursday.
The 1997 fish operation season begins April 10 and runs through August, the period when Columbia Basin salmon are migrating to the ocean.
This spring's runoff is projected to be near the largest on record for the Snake River and in the top 10 of the historical record for the Columbia River.
The runoff will "completely overwhelm the capacity of the turbine system," Bonneville Power Administrator Randy Hardy said.
The high flows also cause high levels of dissolved gas, which can cause problems in fish similar to the bends in human divers.

BPA said it is taking several steps to limit the problem including aggressive marketing of surplus power, extended shutdown of the WNP-2 nuclear plant, extra efforts to keep as many power turbines as possible operating and agreements with operators of other hydropower plants to spread spill volumes as evenly as possible throughout the system.
Last year, utilities accepted anywhere from 200 megawatts (MW) to 1,500 MW of electricity to reduce spill and even more utilities are participating this year, BPA said.
But the Intertie constraints, which were put in place last summer in the wake of two major blackouts, mean the agency cannot sell as much power as it would like to utilities outside of the Northwest.

"We hope the Intertie will be restored to near its full 7,900 megawatt capability for the spring and summer. If not, there may be periods in which energy may need to be spilled because we can't export it out of the region," Hardy said.

The board of the Western Systems Coordinating Council approved plans to raise the capacity by about 25 percent to 6,250 MW earlier this week, and the relability council's full membership is expected to vote on the plan by March 22.
